description:
MT-2c (Sprint 51, F129): the Review "No Rule" screen's COVERED-ITEM SWEEP -- the Sprint 50 fix that runs `_sweepCoveredItems` on EVERY load of the screen rather than only after a bulk action. READ-ONLY and idempotent: navigates, toggles account-filter chips, and selects/deselects rows (transient UI state only). It creates no rules, adds no safe senders, and marks nothing processed, so it is inherently net-zero on the dev DB. SELECTORS AND INTERACTION MODEL VERIFIED LIVE 2026-07-28 against dev build 0.5.8.

WHAT THIS ASSERTS, AND WHY IT NEEDS NO NEW RULE. The sweep's contract is: on every load, drop items now covered by a rule or safe sender, and leave everything else alone. The dev DB already holds 3853 rules and 600 safe senders, so EVERY load of this screen runs the sweep against that full rule set -- the code path is exercised without writing anything. The failure mode worth guarding is OVER-COLLECTION: a sweep that wrongly drops uncovered items, which is exactly the MT-2b/MT-2c bug shape Harold reported in Sprint 50 (items vanishing from the list). This script therefore asserts STABILITY across repeated loads: named rows that are present on the first load must still be present after a Refresh and after a full screen re-entry. If the sweep over-collects, those selectors resolve 0 elements and the run FAILS.

WHY NOT CREATE A RULE FIRST (the obvious design, deliberately rejected 2026-07-28): a create-then-delete variant was written and abandoned after the create path proved hostile to automation on this build -- the Rule Type RadioButton does NOT select via ww_click on either the RadioButton or its parent Group (the form silently stays in its default Entire-Domain mode), the 'Save Rule' button sits off-screen unless the window is maximized (ww_invoke reports success on it WITHOUT pressing it; ww_click correctly errors 'element_offscreen'), and synthetic domains are rejected by input validation so no confirm dialog ever appears. Those are the same obstacles that keep the two F56 create/delete scripts EXCLUDED from the default sweep. Blocking a REAL listed sender was rejected separately: those rows are Harold's live scanned mail, and an item's covered state is not cleanly reversible from the UI, so the script could not honour the Sprint 37 restore-what-you-modify policy. Verifying the sweep's create-side behaviour deterministically belongs in the widget test (`no_rule_review_screen_test`), which already models a pre-existing covering rule and asserts all matching items are removed on the FIRST load with no user action.

HARNESS FACTS (all established by failing runs on 2026-07-28, not assumed):
(1) USE ww_invoke, NOT ww_click, for Buttons -- ww_click reported success WITHOUT activating controls on a cold-launched app. EXCEPTIONS, which must use ww_click with useInvokePattern:false because they do not support InvokePattern: TabBar tabs and static Text nodes ('Element does not support InvokePattern. ControlType: Text') and CheckBoxes, which expose TogglePattern ('...ControlType: CheckBox').
(2) A step reporting success proves DISPATCH, not effect. `ww_assert*` is not replayable by the runner, so every navigation is followed by a step that can only resolve if the app really advanced.
(3) Flutter builds its UIA semantics tree LAZILY in response to a query, not on a timer -- a 10-second wait does NOT help. The leading ww_window_state is the priming query.
(4) ww_invoke does NOT verify visibility: it will report success on an off-screen element without pressing it. ww_click errors 'element_offscreen' instead. Maximize first.

testCases.title: MT-3 entry point opens the screen; the sweep produces a coherent list with named rows

steps._comment: PRIMING QUERY (fact 3) -- also guarantees a maximized window so nothing is off-screen (fact 4).
MT-3: the Review No Rule entry point on the home screen. A resolve failure here means the Sprint 50 MT-3 entry point regressed.

Reaching this screen at all means _loadItems -- and therefore _sweepCoveredItems -- has already run once against the full 3853-rule / 600-safe-sender set. The account chips carry the POST-sweep counts in their accessible names; prefix-matched because counts are data-dependent.

BASELINE ROW A. Each row exposes a 'Select <sender>' checkbox thanks to the Sprint 51 F129 semantics work -- before it, 18 rows were 18 indistinguishable 'checkbox' controls, unusable by screen reader and unaddressable by name. CheckBox needs ww_click (TogglePattern, not InvokePattern -- fact 1). If the dev inbox no longer holds this sender, refresh the name from a live ww_dump_tree and update it in EVERY case below.
PROOF OF EFFECT: 'Clear' is rendered only once a row is genuinely selected, so it proves the checkbox actually toggled rather than the click merely being dispatched. It is also the state restore.
BASELINE ROW B -- a second, different sender, so the assertion is not resting on a single row.

testCases.title: MT-2c CORE: Refresh re-runs the sweep in place -- it must be idempotent, not progressively eat the list

steps._comment: Refresh re-enters _loadItems, so the sweep runs a SECOND time over the same data. The Sprint 50 MT-2b/MT-2c bug shape was items disappearing across reloads; a correct sweep is idempotent.

THE ASSERTION: both baseline rows must SURVIVE the second sweep. Neither sender is covered by any existing rule (they are in the No-Rule list precisely because nothing covers them), so a correct sweep leaves both alone. If the sweep over-collected, these resolve 0 elements and the run FAILS.
A THIRD sweep, to catch a slow leak that a single reload would miss.
The chips must still report coherent post-sweep counts after three sweeps.

testCases.title: MT-2c CORE: full screen re-entry re-runs the sweep from scratch -- rows still survive

steps._comment: Leave the screen entirely and come back. This is the path Harold exercised manually in Sprint 50: a FRESH mount, new state, _loadItems from scratch -- distinct from the in-place Refresh in case 2, and the case where 'the list no longer has the items' was originally reported.
PROOF OF RETURN HOME: the entry point exists only on the home screen.
THE ASSERTION, after a cold re-entry: both rows must still be present.
Teardown: back to home, leaving the screen exactly as found (selection cleared, no filter applied, nothing written).
